about.title: Long Beach Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product should do its job without hurting the person using it. When it doesn't — a space heater that ignites in a Long Beach apartment, a child seat that fails during a collision on Pacific Coast Highway, a power tool that kicks back in a garage off Atlantic Avenue — California law puts the weight on the manufacturer, not on the family left picking up the pieces. Long Beach is home to 474,140 people in Los Angeles County, and defective goods find their way into households in every neighborhood. The rule that matters most here is strict liability: you generally do not have to prove the company was careless, only that the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. We handle product liability claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Hold onto the product, its packaging, and any receipts. Those items frequently become the heart of the claim.

whyChoose.title: Why Long Beach Residents Choose Us for Product Claims

items.title: Strict liability works in your favor
items.desc: In California you typically only need to show the product was defective in design, manufacturing, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. Proving the manufacturer was careless is usually not required.

items.title: More than one company may owe you
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the Long Beach retailer that sold the item can all share responsibility. Our team can sort out who belongs in the claim.

items.title: Evidence-first guidance from day one
items.desc: The product itself is the single most important piece of evidence, and we'll tell you how to keep it safe. We handle these cases on contingency — no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My airbag didn't deploy in a crash on the I-405 in Long Beach. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. Long Beach recorded 2,135 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those involve a vehicle component that failed to perform as designed. If a defective airbag, seat belt, or brake made your injuries worse, a product liability claim against the manufacturer may exist alongside any claim against another driver. We can evaluate whether the part, not just the crash, is part of the story.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Generally, no. California's strict liability approach means the focus is on whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and whether that defect caused your injury. The maker's intentions or level of care usually aren't the deciding factor. That said, every case has its own facts, which is why we review the details.

items.question: I already threw the broken product away. Can I still do anything?
items.answer: You may still have options, so don't assume the claim is over. Photos, receipts, order confirmations, medical records, and any remaining pieces or packaging can help us piece together what happened. If the item is still in a trash bin or with a repair shop, retrieve it if you can. Then contact us and we'll review it at no cost.
